result.question: Why did leprosy break out on Uzziah?

readings.answer: Because the LORD had afflicted him.
readings.support: because the LORD had afflicted him

readings.answer: Because he acted unfaithfully by trying to offer incense reserved for priests.
readings.support: for you have acted unfaithfully | with a censer in his hand to offer incense

readings.answer: Because he raged against the priests.
readings.support: while he raged against the priests | leprosy broke out on his forehead

assessments.reason: It directly quotes the passage’s causal statement, “because the LORD had afflicted him,” which is the same meaning as the key’s “Yahweh struck him.”

The priests state he “acted unfaithfully” by trying to “offer incense” reserved for Aaron’s descendants, and the leprosy follows; this reasonably explains the punishment’s reason, though the text’s explicit cause is that the LORD afflicted him.
The text says “while he raged against the priests … leprosy broke out,” which is temporal, not causal, and then gives the cause: “because the LORD had afflicted him.”
